test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Air India logo consists of:

options.text: a flying swan with the wheel of konark inside it
a flying crane with the wheel of konark inside it
a flying duck with the wheel of konark inside it

solution:
The correct answer is__** a flying swan with the wheel of Konark inside it.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Air India logo** features a stylized flying swan, which symbolizes grace and beauty.
 
• Within the logo, there is a depiction of the **Wheel of Konark**, a famous Sun temple located in Odisha, India.
 
• The design reflects India's rich cultural heritage and its connection to aviation and travel.
 
• The logo was designed to create a strong brand identity for Air India, representing both modernity and tradition.
 
• It is an iconic symbol recognized globally, representing Air India as the national airline of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flying Swan**:

 
 
• The swan is often associated with purity and grace, which aligns with the airline's image as a premier carrier.
 
 
 
• **Wheel of Konark**:
 
 
• The Wheel of Konark, also known as the Sun Wheel, has intricate carvings and symbolizes the eternal cycle of time, often associated with the Sun God, Surya.
 
 
 
• **Brand Identity**:
 
 
• A strong brand identity is crucial for airlines, helping to differentiate them in a competitive market.
 
 
 
• **History**:
 
 
• Air India was founded in 1932 by J.R.D. Tata and has a rich history in Indian aviation, having played a pivotal role in promoting air travel in the country.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition**:
 
 
• Air India is a member of the Star Alliance and operates flights to various international destinations, making its logo widely recognized worldwide.
